title: Modest Savings on Home Loan Refinance Worth It?
body:
With news that HSBC is transferring their Home Loan portfolio to Pepper Money over the next 18 months , I've explored options to jump the gun and refinance. Pepper Money has announced that all HSBC Home Loans being transferred will retain their existing rates, fees, perks, etc, so one option is to do nothing.
My current HSBC interest rate is 6.04% on an owner-occupier, variable rate, principal and interest loan with an offset account. I've spoken to HSBC, and they've let me know they can't offer me a lower rate, despite presenting them with like-for-like products with more competitive rates.
The best offer I'm seeing for a like-for-like (ie. including offset, etc) on my current LVR, and considering factors beyond just the interest rate (ie. establishment fees, ongoing fees, etc) is Up Bank with an Up Home Variable Rate Loan at 5.95% .
However, the savings will be modest. Accounting for everything that is quantifiable (interest savings, current loan discharge including third-party fees, establishment fees, ongoing fee savings, etc), if I were to refinance, my cumulative net savings would be:
$11.61 cumulative net savings after 1 year
$223.23 cumulative net savings after 2 years
$434.84 cumulative net savings after 3 years
My question is simple: if you were in my position, do you think the headache of refinancing (accounting for the time spent on paperwork, admin, and a credit check, etc) is worth it for the cumulative savings above (ie. $434.84 better off after 3 years)? What would you do?
Or are there perhaps other factors I should be considering (particularly with respect to the move to Pepper Money)?
